summary: X and LinkedIn register in the link-owner registry (design/social-per-network/30-link-owner-registry.md, PR 2): a pasted X post/profile link or LinkedIn person/company link, given to web_fetch or media_fetch, is now routed to x_read/linkedin_read instead of reaching the provider or the downloader.
details: web_fetch/media_fetch never change: registering a network is one LinkOwner row (PR 1's own property, now exercised by a real second and third network).

A LinkedIn post link is not claimed (linkedin_read cannot read one from its link; web_fetch may still be able to), and neither are X's or LinkedIn's own shorteners (t.co, lnkd.in) or CDN hosts (pbs.twimg.com, media.licdn.com): all keep reaching the provider as before.
m.linkedin.com is claimed but not readable, the same shape as Instagram's m.instagram.com: the note asks for the www.linkedin.com link instead of naming linkedin_read.
limitations: x_read, linkedin_read and instagram_read keep their own hand-written cross-network branches; replacing those with the registry is PR 3 ("The owners use the registry"), not built here.
